clue.text: Don't take long, girl!

definitions.meaning: an order to be quick, to last no more than an instant
a girl's name, as in Dante's beloved or Benedick's sparring partner

explanation.walkthrough: Split the name as BE A TRICE: a trice is an instant, so 'be a trice' is a jokey order not to take long.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Shrink from chair when lecturer comes in

indicators.note: the lecturer enters the seat, going inside it

parts.note: a bench is a seat, like a chair

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from their seat when the teacher walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: To blench is to flinch or shrink back in fear.

clue.text: Southern band attracting virtually no residents?

definitions.text: Southern band attracting virtually no residents?

parts.words: Southern band attracting virtually no residents?
parts.note: a line of latitude far south, a band round the globe where almost nobody lives

explanation.definitionFit: The polar line of latitude at about 66 degrees south encircles a frozen region with almost no inhabitants.

clue.text: Part of building reported to be cold once upon a time

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a room is part of a building

explanation.surface: A chilly section of an old building is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is an old word for a catarrhal cold or watery discharge.

clue.text: City has box with the insignia of Good Queen Bess

parts.note: a chest is a box

parts.words: the insignia of Good Queen Bess
parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A town owns a casket bearing Elizabeth I's royal cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Queen Bess is Elizabeth I; her cipher was ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, northwest England.

clue.text: Small bits to nibble when aboard ship

indicators.note: being aboard a vessel means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS is steamship
to peck is to nibble at food

explanation.surface: Someone snacks on crumbs while at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny particles or spots are small bits of something.

clue.text: Mechanical device right for cutting length of cloth? The opposite

indicators.note: cutting puts one piece through the middle of another
the opposite reverses which piece cuts which, so the length goes inside

parts.note: proper means right or correct
an ell is an old measure of cloth

explanation.surface: A machine part swaps in for a strip of fabric, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, PROPER would go into ELL; 'The opposite' flips it so ELL goes into PROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A propeller is a bladed rotating device that drives a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Member of the board into PR and democracy, having loosened up

indicators.note: loosening up frees the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A boardroom executive has become relaxed about publicity and democracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A director sits on a firm's board, so is a member of it.

clue.text: Card player and partner in deed that leads to penalty

parts.note: S, South, is one of the four bridge players

indicators.note: the partner goes inside the deed

parts.note: a deed is an action
N, North, is South's bridge partner

explanation.surface: A bridge player and partner do something that earns a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is a penalty imposed for breaking a rule.

clue.text: Prized English horse enthrals this writer

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a steed is a horse
the setter referring to himself gives ME

explanation.surface: A treasured English horse captivates the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Something highly valued or regarded is prized.

clue.text: Funny old fellow in a jacket

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters of the next word behave oddly and get rearranged

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An eccentric old chap is wearing a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolman is a hussar's jacket worn like a cape, or a loose-sleeved robe.

clue.text: One's aberrant regularly?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A child who keeps misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved child, one who routinely misbehaves.

clue.text: Cannon give order to follow vehicle

indicators.note: the order comes after the vehicle, following it in the answer

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone tells a gun crew to fire after the truck.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a cannon, a shot hitting two balls in turn, is called a carom in America.

clue.text: Like Gaul, applying skill to local dispute

parts.note: threep is a Scottish dialect word meaning to argue or quarrel
art is skill

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood row is settled with some craft.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's Gallic War opens 'All Gaul is divided into three parts', hence the definition; 'applying ... to' puts the skill after the dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar described Gaul as divided into three parts, so it was tripartite.

clue.text: One making an impression with other things, that woman

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone impressive arrives with a woman and assorted extras.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver who incises a plate with acid makes an impression from it, a printmaking pun.

clue.text: Star performer, the man to get Ireland excited

parts.note: he refers to a man

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A headline act gets the Irish crowd going.
explanation.definitionFit: The headliner is the main act on a bill, its top performer.

clue.text: Four-in-hand taking count to small house

parts.note: a tally is a count
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A coachman drives his team to a cottage, counting as he goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally-ho was a type of four-in-hand coach, named after the hunting cry.

clue.text: Person at meeting against charge about to be brought in

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the small piece is brought inside the larger one

parts.note: a fee is a charge
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An attendee opposes a fee about to be introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A conferee is someone taking part in a conference.

clue.text: Place for abundant fruit or veg

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Grocers offer either plentiful fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is planted with fruit trees, where fruit grows in plenty.

clue.text: Wild animal runs south of river

indicators.note: in a down clue the runs come below the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A creature dashes along beneath a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer is a wild hoofed animal.

clue.text: Outdoor party doll?

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for a barbecue held outside

explanation.definitionFit: Barbie is both Australian slang for a barbecue gathering and the brand of fashion doll.

clue.text: Nevertheless, many may be at work in hotel

definitions.text: may be at work in hotel

parts.note: but means nevertheless
tons means a great many

explanation.surface: However, lots of staff could be busy at the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttons is the old name for a uniformed pageboy, from his jacket's rows of buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageboy in a hotel, nicknamed for his buttoned uniform, would be at work there.

clue.text: Material that's marvellous — plush, not hard

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous, marvellous

indicators.note: the abbreviation for hard is dropped

parts.note: plush means rich and luxurious

explanation.surface: Wonderful cloth: luxurious but soft.
explanation.walkthrough: H is hard, as on pencils; dropping it leaves RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, a woven material.

clue.text: Most gathered to have short celebration either side of stream

indicators.note: the shortened celebration sits on both sides of the stream, enclosing it
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a fiesta is a festive celebration
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A big crowd assembles for a brief party beside a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' leaves FIEST; 'gathered' suggests a crowd, but here it is the dressmaker's sense of fabric drawn into ruffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that is frilled is gathered into ruffles, so the frilliest is the most gathered.

clue.text: Religious novice embraced by Michelangelo

indicators.note: the letters wanted are held within the artist's name

explanation.surface: A young monk is hugged by the great Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a chela is a disciple or pupil of a guru, a religious novice.

clue.text: Trick to take in companion initially

indicators.note: the companion is put first, at the start

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour
to eat is to take in food

explanation.surface: A con involving inviting a friend to lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat is to trick or deceive someone.

clue.text: French writer at home getting into the groove

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, going inside it

parts.note: a race is a groove, as in the channel of a ball bearing
in means at home

explanation.surface: A French author settles into a comfortable routine at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was the great French tragic dramatist of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Spy, not totally serious, who may disturb women?

parts.note: a mole is a spy inside an organisation

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: stern means serious

explanation.surface: A rather grave secret agent bothers the ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: A molester harasses or assaults people, women among the likeliest victims.

clue.text: Niche accommodating half of the male ducks beside river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: only the front half of the word is used

parts.note: male ducks are drakes

explanation.surface: A nesting box houses some drakes by the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe flows through Devon to Exeter; 'beside' places the drakes' first half after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exedra is a recess or alcove with seating, a niche that can accommodate people.

clue.text: Obscure Tories being devious in the City

indicators.note: the scrambled party members sit inside the postcode, held within it

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: devious behaviour twists things, so the word's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Conservatives in the Square Mile behave in shady, mysterious ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a few, hence obscure.
